{{Infobox person|image=Richard_Dickinson_Chambers.gif}}

'''Richard Dickinson Chambers''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (16 March 1935 — 18 April 2019) was a British organofluorine chemist. He was Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at [[Durham University]].<ref name="sandford">{{Cite journal|last=Sandford|first=Graham|title=Richard Dickinson Chambers. 16 March 1935 — 18 April 2019|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2020.0036|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|year=2021 |volume=70|pages=107–130 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0036 |s2cid=229355290 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

From [[West Stanley]], Chambers studied chemistry at [[Durham University]] and joined the faculty of the Department of Chemistry in 1960. He retired in 2000. By the time of his retirement he had supervised 96 PhD students to completion, among them [[Jack Cunningham, Baron Cunningham of Felling|Lord Cunningham of Felling]] and [[Tristram Chivers]].<ref name=sandford /><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Chivers |first=Tristram |title=Some bentafluorophenyl derivatives of tin and boron |type=PhD thesis |publisher=Durham University |year=1964 |url=https://etheses.dur.ac.uk/8909/1/8909_5840.PDF?UkUDh:CyT |access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref>

In 1997 he was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] and in 2003 his [[fluorine]] research was recognised with the Prix Henri Moissan from the [[Maison de la chimie|Maison de la Chimie]] in Paris.
